name: Incident optical stimulus at a cone photoreceptor
summary: Incident photons reaching a cone photoreceptor provide the physical optical input to phototransduction. The stimulus spectrum is intentionally left unspecified because the cited physiology establishes photon-driven transduction without defining a single canonical spectral distribution.

system.name: Optical field incident on a cone photoreceptor

axis.notes: Optical spectral coordinate; no single stimulus spectrum is implied by the physiology reference.

constraints: spectral distribution depends on the external visual stimulus
this record represents the physical photon input rather than the CIE standard-observer response curve

target_ref.label: Cone photoreceptor electrical response to light

relationships.description: Photon absorption initiates the phototransduction cascade that produces a graded cone membrane-potential response.

sources.title: Phototransduction
sources.publisher: NCBI Bookshelf, National Library of Medicine

evidence.derivation: The physiology source establishes photon-driven phototransduction but does not define one canonical stimulus spectrum, so Atlas leaves the optical spectral profile unresolved rather than substituting the CIE sensitivity curve for the physical stimulus.
